adf7ef1a01.q: How long did Brad Morrill's search and acquisition journey take from leaving Crystal Flash to closing on Richfield Trailer Supply?
adf7ef1a01.a: Brad left Crystal Flash on June 1, 2024, and closed on Richfield Trailer Supply exactly two years later on June 1, 2026. While the official search journey was 19 months from kickoff to close, the total journey including the five-month acquisition course and planning period was two years to the day.

c495efe5a0.q: What was Brad Morrill's acquisition funnel from initial deal sourcing to closing Richfield Trailer Supply?
c495efe5a0.a: Calder Capital brought 65 deals, while Brad sourced 20 independently for approximately 85 total in the top of funnel. He had initial conversations with 45-50 owners, conducted deep dives into 15 businesses, made five IOI/LOI offers, and ultimately closed on the fifth one, Richfield Trailer Supply.

f555a4d8c4.q: What was Brad Morrill's purchase price and down payment strategy for acquiring Richfield Trailer Supply?
f555a4d8c4.a: Brad had $500,000 to $600,000 of immediate personal cash available before considering family and friends or investors. Operating as a self-funded searcher with an SBA loan structure at 10% down, he targeted a $4 to $5 million valuation range, calculated from a $1 million EBITDA at approximately a four multiple.

40d00af8cd.q: What geographic parameters did Brad Morrill set for sourcing Richfield Trailer Supply?
40d00af8cd.a: Brad restricted his search to within an hour to 75 minutes of Grand Rapids, Michigan, which included the lakeshore, Muskegon, Holland, Kalamazoo, Battle Creek, Lansing, and the Grand Rapids area. As the search progressed, he adjusted these parameters and ultimately found Richfield Trailer Supply in Flint, Michigan, located 1 hour 45 minutes from his home.

d0c41a3a7d.q: Why did Brad Morrill rule out manufacturing businesses during his search for Richfield Trailer Supply?
d0c41a3a7d.a: Brad ruled out manufacturing because he lacked direct experience in manufacturing plants and wanted to focus on areas where he was already up to speed. He also noted that competitive pressure from others seeking manufacturing businesses was high. When he did visit a manufacturing prospect selling into automotive and appliance industries, the unknown variables and cyclical customer dynamics made the risk profile too high compared to distribution and service businesses.
